reference_title: Drilled Shafts: Construction Procedures and LRFD Design Methods
chapter_title: Design of Groups of Drilled Shafts

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Groups of drilled shafts may be required when axial or lateral loads are too large for a single shaft, when a pile cap foundation is used, or when redundancy is desired. Group behavior differs from single shaft behavior due to interaction effects — overlapping stress zones reduce individual shaft capacity and increase settlement. Design of groups involves: geotechnical strength limit state (group capacity vs. individual capacity); service limit state (group settlement and lateral deflection); structural design of cap.
key_points: Groups used when single shaft insufficient for load or when cap foundation preferred
Group interaction: overlapping stress zones reduce capacity and increase settlement vs. individual shaft
Design checks: group geotechnical strength, group settlement, group lateral deflection, cap structural design
sections.applicability: Groups of two or more drilled shafts; pile cap foundations

sections.title: Group Versus Single Shaft Foundation
sections.body: Single shaft (monoshaft) advantages: no pile cap needed; smaller footprint; no cap excavation; lower cost when axial loads moderate and lateral capacity sufficient. Multiple shaft groups with cap advantages: greater capacity for large loads; rotational stiffness from cap; redundancy; better for large lateral loads where single shaft diameter would be impractical. Selection criteria: cost (foundation + cap); schedule; constructability; redundancy requirements; site constraints.
key_points: Single shaft: no cap, smaller footprint, lower cost for moderate loads
Group with cap: greater capacity, rotational stiffness, redundancy for large loads
Evaluation criteria: cost including cap, schedule, constructability, redundancy
sections.applicability: Foundation type selection; monoshaft vs. group decision

sections.title: Considerations for Spacing
sections.body: Minimum center-to-center spacing per AASHTO: 2.5B for compression groups (where B = shaft diameter); 3.0B for uplift groups to reduce interaction effects. Practical minimum: 3D (3× diameter) provides significantly better efficiency than 2.5D for most soils. Effects of closer spacing: reduced group efficiency (lower total capacity); increased group settlement; more difficult concrete placement between shafts; reduced effectiveness of integrity testing. Closer spacing may be acceptable if: group efficiency is verified by load testing; the reduced capacity is compensated by additional shaft length; construction is carefully sequenced to avoid interference.
key_points: AASHTO minimum spacing: 2.5B (compression groups); 3.0B (uplift groups)
Practical minimum: 3B provides significantly better efficiency than 2.5B
Closer spacing: reduced efficiency, increased settlement, construction difficulty
sections.applicability: Group layout design; cap design coordination

sections.title: Group Effects on Axial Resistance
sections.body: Group efficiency η = (group capacity)/(n × individual shaft capacity). Two failure modes: (1) individual shaft failure — each shaft fails separately; capacity = η × sum of individual shaft capacities; efficiency factor <1 typically in cohesive soils, may be >1 in cohesionless soils due to densification during installation; AASHTO: η = 0.65 for 3B spacing in cohesive soils, 1.0 in cohesionless soils for typical spacing; (2) block failure — shafts and enclosed soil fail as a unit; block capacity = perimeter shear × depth + base area × net bearing pressure; governs for closely spaced groups in cohesive soils. Design uses lesser of (1) or (2) — block failure typically governs for close spacing in clay. Group settlement: elastic compression (self-weight of cap and shafts); consolidation settlement of compressible soils below pile tips; secondary compression. Group settlement analysis: equivalent footing method — distribute load over equivalent area at 2/3 of embedded depth; use Terzaghi-Meyerhof-DeBeer correction for shape and depth. AASHTO: settlement under service load ≤ tolerable differential settlement (structure-dependent).
key_points: Two failure modes: individual shaft failure (with efficiency η) or block failure
AASHTO efficiency factor η: 0.65 for 3B spacing in cohesive soils; 1.0 in cohesionless soils
Block failure governs for closely spaced groups in clay
Group settlement: elastic + consolidation + secondary; analyzed via equivalent footing method
Service limit: settlement ≤ tolerable differential settlement for the structure
equations: Group capacity by individual failure: Qgroup = η × Σ(individual shaft capacities)
Block failure: Qblock = (perimeter × average su × depth) + (base area × Nc*su)
sections.applicability: Axial capacity and settlement of drilled shaft groups in all geomaterial types

sections.title: Group Effects in Lateral Loading
sections.body: P-multiplier (fm) concept: in a group, leading row shafts carry more load than trailing row shafts due to shadow effects. P-multipliers reduce the p-y curves of individual shafts within the group relative to a single isolated shaft. AASHTO p-multipliers fm: leading row = 0.8; second row = 0.4; third and subsequent rows = 0.3 for 3B spacing; increase toward 1.0 as spacing increases toward 5-6B. Computer programs: FB-Multipier (recommended by FHWA), GROUP; PLAXIS. Group analysis: apply p-multiplier to each shaft's p-y curves; analyze group as system with cap stiffness; distribute lateral load and moment to individual shafts based on relative stiffness. Interaction effects reduce total lateral resistance and increase deflections compared to n times single shaft resistance.
key_points: P-multiplier (fm): reduces p-y resistance for group shafts; leading row fm=0.7, second row fm=0.5, third+ rows fm=0.35 at 3B spacing
P-multipliers approach 1.0 as spacing increases to 5-6B
Computer programs: FB-Multipier (FHWA recommended), GROUP
Group lateral resistance < n × single shaft resistance due to shadow effects
sections.applicability: Lateral capacity of drilled shaft groups; p-multiplier method

sections.title: Combined Loading and Computation of Load Distribution to Group
sections.body: Methods for distributing combined column loads (axial, shear, moment) to individual shafts in a group: (1) Simple static equilibrium — rigid cap assumption; load distribution based on statics; applicable for small groups with simple loading; (2) Simple elastic solution — cap assumed rigid; shaft load proportional to distance from centroid for eccentric axial load; lateral loads distributed equally; moments distributed in proportion to shaft stiffness; (3) Nonlinear computer solution — model individual shafts with p-y curves and t-z curves; cap modeled as rigid or flexible element; iterative solution for load distribution; most rigorous. AASHTO: use method appropriate for load complexity and group size. For large groups with eccentric loading or combined loading, nonlinear computer analysis recommended.
key_points: Simple static equilibrium: rigid cap, statics only; for small groups simple loading
Simple elastic solution: rigid cap, load proportional to distance from centroid
Nonlinear computer solution: most rigorous; required for large groups or complex combined loading
Computer programs: FB-Multipier, GROUP, OpenSees for nonlinear group analysis
sections.applicability: Load distribution to individual shafts in groups under combined loading

sections.title: Summary
sections.body: Chapter provided guidance on design of groups of drilled shafts for axial and lateral loading including group efficiency, block failure, group settlement, p-multipliers for lateral loading, and methods for load distribution to individual shafts. Use n × individual shaft capacity with efficiency factor or block failure (whichever governs) for axial group strength limit state. Apply p-multipliers for lateral group effects. Nonlinear computer analysis recommended for large or complex groups.
